title: Minimum Sum of Mountain Triplets II
statement:
You are given an integer array `nums`. Three indices `i < j < k` form a mountain when the middle value is strictly larger than both outer ones: `nums[i] < nums[j]` and `nums[k] < nums[j]`. The sum of a mountain is `nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k]`.

Return the smallest sum over all mountains in `nums`, or `-1` if `nums` contains no mountain.
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every triple is O(n³), far too slow for `10^5` numbers. Fix the peak `j` instead. The best partners are then the smallest value anywhere to its left and the smallest value anywhere to its right: they make the sum as small as possible, and if even they are not below `nums[j]`, no other value on that side is. So each peak needs only two minimums, which prefix and suffix minimums give in O(1).

## Approach

1. Build `suffixMin` from the right: `suffixMin[k]` is the smallest value from index `k` to the end.
2. Sweep `j` from `1` to `n - 2`, keeping `prefixMin`, the smallest value before `j`.
3. Let `left = prefixMin` and `right = suffixMin[j + 1]`. If both are below `nums[j]`, the triple is a mountain; keep the smaller of `best` and its sum.
4. Fold `nums[j]` into `prefixMin` before moving on.
5. Return `best`, or `-1` if no peak worked.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [8, 6, 1, 5, 3]` gives `suffixMin = [1, 1, 1, 3, 3]`.
- `j = 1` (6): `left = 8` is not smaller, skip; `prefixMin` becomes 6.
- `j = 2` (1): `left = 6` is not smaller, skip; `prefixMin` becomes 1.
- `j = 3` (5): `left = 1`, `right = 3`, both smaller: sum `1 + 5 + 3 = 9`.

The answer is `9`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass builds `suffixMin`, one pass tries every peak.
- Space: O(n) for `suffixMin`.

## Pitfalls

- Both comparisons are strict: equal neighbours, as in `[1, 1, 1]`, do not form a mountain.
- `right` must come from `j + 1` onwards, and `prefixMin` must be updated only after `j` is used, or `nums[j]` could pair with itself.
- Return `-1`, not `Infinity`, when no mountain exists.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `suffixMin[k]` | smallest value in `nums[k..n-1]` |
| `prefixMin` | smallest value before the current peak `j` |
| `j` | index of the candidate peak |
| `left`, `right` | the best outer values for this peak |
| `best` | smallest mountain sum found so far |

narration.3: suffixMin will hold, for each index, the smallest value from there to the end.
narration.5: Fill it from right to left so each entry reuses the one after it.
narration.6: The minimum from k onward is nums[k] or the minimum from k + 1 onward.
narration.8: No mountain has been found yet.
narration.9: prefixMin is the smallest value strictly before the current peak.
narration.10: Try every index that has at least one value on each side as the peak.
narration.11: The best left partner is the smallest value before j.
narration.12: The best right partner is the smallest value after j.
narration.13: Both partners must be strictly smaller than the peak.
narration.14: This is a mountain; keep its sum if it is the smallest so far.
narration.16: Now nums[j] lies to the left of every later peak.
narration.18: Report the smallest sum, or -1 when no peak had smaller values on both sides.
